clues: This town sits on the banks of a great river in the Amazon lands of Brazil. The big city of Manaus lies a short drive away to the east.
Heat here eases in a strange way for the deep rain forest. Cool drops come often, and nights feel much less hot than the days.
It was founded in 1786, from a Mura village on the left bank of the river. The village had been calmed just one year before, in 1785.
A famed folk dance fest draws crowds to this river town each year. The town is one of the most seen spots in the whole rain forest zone.
Its main landmark is a church named for Our Lady of Nazareth. She is the town patron saint, and her church crowns the town heart.
